decisions.reason: The client identifies WROOM-1 as the selected ESP32-S3 module whose exposed-pin constraints govern the GPIO mapping.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Sorry, GPIO3 was from my original ESP32 design — mistake on my side. For 5V_EN you can use GPIO5. Also I realized GPIO22, 23, 25, 27 are not exposed on the WROOM-1 module, so I need to reassign SCL0 (GPIO22→38), SPI MOSI (GPIO23→26). I'll update the docs and send you the full updated GPIO table.

decisions.reason: The existing same-message MODIFY already fully records the required change from GPIO3 to GPIO5 for 5V_EN.
Changing GPIO assignments does not alter the DCDC1 voltage, current rating, or normal-operation role.
The standalone USB supply behavior and source-selection rules do not depend on the reassigned GPIOs.
The current standby-power rule explicitly names GPIO3 as the controller for 5V_EN, which the client reassigns to GPIO5.

decisions.reason: The sensor-board fanout role remains unchanged and its state contains no physical GPIO assignments.
The charge-status interface uses GPIO13 and is unaffected by the 5V_EN, SCL0, and SPI MOSI reassignments.
The GPIO changes do not alter the battery-protection controller, cutoff thresholds, or protection components.
The NTC connection and AXP2101 thermal-protection behavior are independent of the reassigned GPIOs.
The source changes controller pin assignments but not the AXP2101 power source, battery range, or load coverage.
GPIO reassignment does not change the number, separation, or functional identity of the project boards.
The connector pinout names logical nets such as SCL0 and 5V_EN; changing their ESP32 GPIO endpoints does not change the connector signals or pin order.
